evals.name: routing-triggers
evals.prompt: /r:task-quick the export button posts twice when you double-click it
evals.expected_output: task-quick loads and runs in this one thread: a scope check first (hand it to task-run if it needs a design decision, a risk surface, a migration or more than about five files), then test-first implementation with the build green, then the real Codex reviewer over the finished diff, then each finding verified against the code as confirmed or dismissed with a reason, and only the confirmed ones fixed. It ends with the diff uncommitted on the current branch — no plan file, no branch, no PR, no commit.

evals.name: routing-excludes-task-run
evals.prompt: implement issue #42 end to end and open a PR for it
evals.expected_output: task-run's job: a task shipped behind a PR wants the feature branch, the explored and Codex-reviewed plan, and the whole /r:task-review pipeline. task-quick must not load — it has no planning phase, never branches, never commits and never opens a PR, and its single Codex pass is not the review a shipped change is owed.

evals.name: routing-excludes-task-review
evals.prompt: review the diff I already have and fix what it finds
evals.expected_output: task-review's job: the code already exists, so there is nothing to implement. task-quick must not load — its first step would have nothing to do, and its single Codex pass plus verification is a thinner review than a finished diff deserves.

evals.name: routing-excludes-issues-fix
evals.prompt: work through issues.md and fix everything on the list
evals.expected_output: A whole backlog is issues-fix's job — it verifies each item against the code, groups what one change can fix together, and keeps going when a group fails. task-quick must not load: it takes exactly one small change and has no loop, no grouping and no per-item bookkeeping.

evals.name: routing-triggers-quick-phrasing
evals.prompt: small change, don't run the whole pipeline: rename the userId param on OrderController.confirm to buyerId
evals.expected_output: task-quick loads: this is the shape it exists for — one or two files, no design decision, no risk surface. It implements test-first, builds, gets a real Codex read of the diff, verifies each finding and fixes only the ones that hold, rather than paying for task-run's explorers, plan review and full post-task review.
